chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from some of his companions, from Musaddif, who said:

A boil (dammal) broke out on me, so I would prostrate on one side. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saw its mark and said, 'What is this?' I said, 'I cannot prostrate fully because of the boil, so I prostrate tilted.' He said to me, 'Do not do that. Dig a small pit and place the boil in the pit so that you can place your forehead on the ground.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اَللَهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.حَفِيرَة: Small pit or hole dug in the ground
key_terms.دُمَّل: Boil or large pustule on the skin

ai.seo_question: How should one perform prostration if a boil or wound prevents the forehead from touching the ground?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the principle of *raf' al-haraj* (removal of hardship) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a practical physical modification rather than a concession to omit the pillar. By instructing the companion to dig a pit for the boil, the Imam ensures that the forehead remains in direct contact with the earth, preserving the essential condition (*shart*) of *sujood* while accommodating the medical impediment. This highlights the Shia emphasis on maintaining the literal form of worship whenever possible, even if it requires minor physical effort.
